conflict_resolutions.WHOLE_END_ACTOR_DISAGREEMENT: Executive Order 14148 revokes the order as a whole by name on its signing date, 2025-01-20. The other actors named by the machine record are same-day concurrent revocations or supersessions of conflicting provisions dated 2025-01-20, or later recitals, each described in the source notes; none gives a date earlier than 2025-01-20 and none is needed for the first end, which is taken from Executive Order 14148.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held registered text of Executive Order 14082 is the official Federal Register text layer at 87 FR 56861, PDF pages 1-4 (Federal Register / Vol. 87, No. 179 / Friday, September 16, 2022); it names Executive Order 14082 of September 12, 2022, Implementation of the Energy and Infrastructure Provisions of the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, and runs from the title to the signature block. The complete clause inventory was checked against the numbered section headings of that text. Section 2(xx) of Executive Order 14148 of January 20, 2025 (Initial Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions, 90 FR 8237, Federal Register of January 28, 2025) lists Executive Order 14082 of September 12, 2022 among the executive actions that section 2 declares hereby revoked. The held text of Executive Order 14148 states no effective date later than its signing, so the revocation operates from its signing date, 2025-01-20. Whole-order revocation by name is the first end of every clause that had not already been exhausted by performance. The order has no other ending instrument before 2025-01-20 in the packet's later-event chain, which for this order lists besides Executive Order 14148: Executive Order 14096 and Executive Order 14154. Each such instrument is recorded in the source notes with its date and why it is not an earlier end; none reinstates this order. The packet's name search of held order texts for this order's number returned, among texts dated on or after 2025-01-20, only Executive Order 14148 and Executive Order 14154. The later-source search is recorded by the three machine searches selected on the sheet: the U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09), the eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with the CFR bulk files, and the Federal Register executive-order disposition catalog; their coverage statements were read and each is marked complete. Savings are addressed in the savings statement. The first end of the whole order is 2025-01-20.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Checked whether any clause ended before 2025-01-20. The held own text of Executive Order 14082 contains no provision that terminates or sets an expiry date for the order or for any clause; deadlines in clauses are performance dates, not ends. Clauses that revoke or amend earlier instruments in the present tense were executed on the order's own date and are recorded as ended by performance on that date; every other clause ended on 2025-01-20. No earlier revocation, supersession or amendment that ends a clause is shown in the packet's later-event chain; the instruments it lists other than Executive Order 14148 are addressed in the clause reasons and source notes.","independent_command_check":"Every clause recorded for Executive Order 14082 is a statement or command of that order itself. Statutes, regulations and other instruments that the order cites keep whatever force they have independently of it, but they are not clauses of the order, so no independent command keeps any clause running after the revocation.","savings_check":"Savings were examined in the order's own text and in Executive Order 14148: section 2 contains no saving clause for the revoked orders, section 3(b) leaves existing actions to later review, and section 4 saves only statutory authority and Office of Management and Budget functions. The state is transferred_or_accrued for actions already taken, with no specific surviving action identified from held sources.","scope_check":"Section 2 of Executive Order 14148 revokes the order as a whole by number and by title, without limiting words and without excepting any clause, so the ending is not confined to part of the order. Section 4(a) of Executive Order 14148 states that nothing in it impairs the authority granted by law to an agency or the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget; that preserves statutory authority and does not preserve any clause of this order."}

savings.reason: Section 3(b) of Executive Order 14148 directs the Director of the Domestic Policy Council and the Director of the National Economic Council to review all Federal Government actions taken pursuant to the orders, memoranda and proclamations listed in section 2 and to take necessary steps to rescind, replace or amend such actions as appropriate. Because rescission of actions already taken is left to later action, Federal actions already taken under Executive Order 14082 before 2025-01-20 were not themselves revoked by section 2 and stood until rescinded, replaced or amended individually. No held source identifies a particular surviving action or its later fate, so none is asserted. The earlier instruments revoked or amended by the clauses executed on the order's own date stay revoked or amended: those acts are accrued effects not undone by section 2 of Executive Order 14148, except that the instruments amended, Executive Orders 14008 and 14052, are themselves revoked by section 2 of Executive Order 14148, while Executive Order 12898 is not listed in section 2 of that order, so text inserted into it by section 4(b) was not revoked by it and its later fate is not traced in the held sources of this packet.

source_notes.date_qualification: 2025-01-20: same signing date as EO 14148; the order of signing within that day is not established.
source_notes.reason: Section 4(a) of Executive Order 14154 of 2025-01-20 (90 FR 8353) lists this order among executive orders that are revoked and states that any offices established in them are abolished. It bears the same date as EO 14148, so it is a concurrent express revocation that cannot make the first end of any clause earlier than 2025-01-20.

source_notes.date_qualification: 2023-04-21: restates text that section 4(b) of this order had inserted into Executive Order 12898; not an end.
source_notes.reason: Section 7(a) of Executive Order 14096 of 2023-04-21 (88 FR 25251) restates section 1-102(b) of Executive Order 12898 as amended by section 4(b) of Executive Order 14082, replacing the text inserted by that section. It changes text in Executive Order 12898 and does not amend, supersede or revoke any command of Executive Order 14082 itself; section 4(b) of Executive Order 14082 had already been performed on 2022-09-12. It is therefore not an end of any clause of Executive Order 14082.
